tier_reason: The only speed figures come from Tests/Speed/Speed.cpp, which ignores Trace()'s return value and the reject counters and passes no sink, so without a reachable Baical server every call fails after the mutex and dropped calls are reported as throughput; the pool is sized to hold every record, the timer stops before delivery, and the published 5,210,000/s figure matches no whole-millisecond reading of that loop (different build). Directional only.

corrections.caveats: First-party enqueue-only measurement with a flawed harness (ignores rejected calls, 64 MB pool, no delivery timed, whole-ms timer); baselines not like for like (vsprintf with 6 args vs one deferred integer). Abandoned port at v5.2.0; LGPL-3.0-or-later.

tier_reason: First-party 2012 press numbers stay tier C; the 1000x-vs-syslog claim was never measured and the README figure disagrees with doc/performence.txt.

corrections.caveats: '1000x faster than syslog' is unmeasured; press harnesses asymmetric (84-byte lines across procs x threads vs bare 'loglog' single-thread), rsyslogd config undocumented; README 250k/s vs doc/performence.txt ~430k/s (v1.1.1) and ~900k/s (v1.1.0), all 2012. Sync path takes a global rwlock, stat(2) and write(2) per call; use_writer_thread drops on a full 4 KB FIFO.
